finding.claim: purge() calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so any authenticated user can run purgeAll() without admin permission (broken authorization).
finding.source: Any authenticated HTTP request to the purge handler; the user comes from the request context via userFrom(r) and has no admin perm.
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) obtains the caller's user
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins, but the result is ignored

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a bool and does not write an error or abort. No other guard, middleware or early return exists in purge(). Compare rotateKeys at line 33, which correctly uses the result of mustPerm and returns on failure. That function is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12 only returns a bool; its result is discarded at handlers.go:26; no middleware or other guard in the code available)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, discarding its bool (defined at handlers.go:12-14, which neither aborts nor writes an error), so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
